Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

according to preposition

in keeping with, as laid down by

also in accordance with, in keeping with, in line with, according to plan, according to the law

classical

Liv. 1.26.5: secundum lēgem faciō
Cic. Fin. 4.26: illī brevius secundum nātūram vīvere
Traupman 178: secundum lēgem, according to the law

secundum + acc.

according to, in keeping with

With a person it means in someone’s favour: pontificēs secundum sē dēcrēvisse, that the pontiffs had decided for him (Cic. Att. 4.2.3, Lewis & Short). For “according to” a source, see the other sense.

Other words

  • ex + abl. — in accordance with, under

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 5.21.1: ex sententiā nāvigāsse; Traupman 185, 270: ex foedere, according to the terms of the agreement

    ex lēge, ex foedere; ex sententiā, as one wished, as planned.

Examples

  • et conlaudāvī secundum facta et virtūtēs tuās

    and I praised you as your deeds and merits deserveTer. Eun. 1090

  • nāta est sententia veterum Acadēmicōrum et Peripatēticōrum, ut fīnem bonōrum dīcerent secundum nātūram vīvere

    so arose the view of the Old Academy and the Peripatetics, who said that the highest good was to live according to natureCic. Fin. 2.34

  • rēbus tuīs tōtōque itinere ex sententiā cōnfectō nōs quam prīmum revīsās

    when your business and the whole journey have gone according to plan, come back to us as soon as you canCic. Att. 4.14.2

See also according to, agreement, law.
